Slide 1 · Title

TwinForge AI

Your factory. Reimagined before reality.

An agentic industrial digital twin on Google Cloud. It mirrors a factory as a live model, spots trouble early, simulates the alternatives and proposes a plan, which a person approves before anything changes.

Vertex AI · Gemini Agent Development Kit Firebase App Hosting Cloud Run Secret Manager Cloud Storage
Live: twinforge--twin-forge.asia-southeast1.hosted.app Code: github.com/The-OWLabs/twin-forge-ai Region: asia-southeast1 (Singapore) Version: 16 October 2026
Speaker notes: TwinForge turns a factory into a living model that AI agents can reason about safely. Everything you'll see runs live on Google Cloud.
Slide 2 · Executive summary

Executive summary

TwinForge AI gives a plant team one place to see the whole factory, understand what is going wrong, compare what to do about it, and act with confidence.

See

A live digital twin of lines, machines, materials, orders, cameras and mobile robots, in topology, isometric, floor-plan and 3D views.

Understand

Six specialist AI agents investigate incidents, and a multi-agent copilot built with Google's Agent Development Kit answers questions with traceable figures.

Decide

A deterministic plant engine simulates the options; a person approves the plan, the twin executes it, and every step is audited.

Slide 3 · The problem

Factories decide too late, with too little context

Signals are scattered

Machine health, quality, materials and customer orders live in separate systems. A failing robot, a quality drift and a short component look like three unrelated problems.

Decisions are reactive

Teams find out when a line stops. Comparing "keep running", "stop for maintenance" and "move work to another line" by hand takes hours they don't have.

Generic AI is unsafe here

A chatbot that invents a number, or acts on equipment by itself, is a liability on a shop floor. Operations need traceable figures and a human in charge.

Digital twins are slow to build

Modelling a plant traditionally takes specialists and months, so most plants never get a twin they can use.
Speaker notes: The cost of a late decision compounds: a trip on one robot can starve a line, miss a critical order and waste energy at the same time.
Slide 4 · Our solution

One loop: observe, investigate, simulate, decide, learn

Observe→Investigate→Predict→Simulate→Recommend→Human approval→Execute and audit

Live digital twin

Every page renders from one shared factory state, so the dashboard, the twin, the agents and the simulator always agree.

Agents with evidence

Each finding lists its inputs, method, evidence and confidence. The copilot shows every tool call and checks every figure.

What-if on the twin

Plans are simulated on the same plant model and scored on delivery, cost, risk and sustainability.

People decide

Agents can only propose. Approve, reject and roll back are human actions, recorded in the audit trail.

Build any plant

The Twin Builder drafts a twin from a drawing and a description; the Playground lets you place assets and set rules.

Open by design

The same tools are served over the Model Context Protocol, so other agents can work with the twin, and still only propose.
Slide 5 · Demo storyline

The crisis: a robot is failing just as a critical order is due

Aurora Electronics, Plant 2 (Pune) runs two PCB assembly lines and a packaging line. Robot A-ROB-03 on Assembly Line A develops bearing damage while order ORD-1042 for Kestrel Robotics is due and the MCU-7 microcontroller is in short supply.

What the twin finds (model estimates on demo data)

PlanScore / 100Late unitsEstimated costUnplanned stop
Reference plan (asset assumed healthy)100.00$7.4KNone
Continue production45.7711$57.6KTrip at about h+16.5
Stop for preventive maintenance72.5471$20.6KNone
Reroute to Line B + maintain (recommended)82.20$13.7KNone

Scores weight delivery 40, cost 30, risk 20 and sustainability 10 against the reference plan. Figures come from the plant model at the start of the crisis.

Slide 6 · Presenter script (5 minutes)

Live demo, step by step

Start from Demo controls → Run Factory Crisis Demo. A guided panel walks through each step.

  1. Command Center. A critical incident appears. OEE, output, health, energy, scrap, shortages and delivery risk all update from the same state; ORD-1042 shows about 700 units at risk.
  2. AI Operations. Six agents run OBSERVE → INVESTIGATE → PREDICT → SIMULATE → RECOMMEND. Each stage streams its real results: anomalies, findings with evidence, the no-action forecast and the ranked plans.
  3. What-If Simulator. Compare four plans. Move a lever, for example MCU-7 usable stock, and every plan recalculates instantly.
  4. Digital Twin Studio. The recommended plan's path is highlighted. Switch to 3D, orbit the plant and watch the mobile robots.
  5. Approvals. Review actions, evidence, risks and rollback. Approve, then fast-forward 8 hours: Line B takes over, A-ROB-03 is maintained and returns healthy, and the incident closes.
  6. Audit Trail. Every alert, finding, scenario, decision and resulting change is listed with links.
  7. Visual Quality and CCTV. Line A's reject rate tracks the robot's vibration (r ≈ 0.89). In the CCTV Control Room, put real factory footage on every camera and run a visual check.
  8. Twin Builder and Playground. Describe a new plant and review the draft, or drag machines and robots onto the floor, add rules, preview in 3D and apply.
  9. Copilot. Ask "Why is Line A rejecting more boards?" The coordinator delegates to specialist agents, shows every tool call and checks every figure. Ask it to propose the plan: it pauses for your confirmation.
Speaker notes: Keep the guided panel open; it carries the story. Reset Demo restores the starting state at any time.

Slide 9 · What-If Simulator

Compare plans on the twin before touching the plant

  • Four plans side by side: reference, continue, preventive maintenance, reroute + maintain, plus a custom plan.
  • More than ten levers: maintenance start and duration, robot speed, line allocation, component availability, expediting, order quantity and priority, repair duration, energy price, idle draw, horizon.
  • Results recalculate instantly because the same engine runs in the browser.
  • Each plan lists its assumptions; machines are calibrated from telemetry, never from hidden ground truth.
Slide 10 · Digital Twin Studio

Four views of one live twin, including real-time 3D

  • Topology (lines, machines, sensors, materials, orders), Isometric, Floor plan and 3D, all rendered from the same layout.
  • Click any machine, rack, truck, camera or robot for live telemetry, diagnostics, history, dependencies and documents.
  • Mobile robots (AMRs, AGVs, forklifts, tuggers) carry kits and pallets; their trips follow line output, and they park with the reason when a line stops.
  • The 3D view loads only when opened, and adapts its quality to the device.
Slide 11 · Approvals and audit

A person approves; the twin executes; everything is recorded

  • Each recommendation shows its actions, evidence, benefits, risks, impact and how to roll it back.
  • Approval turns the plan into directives (maintenance window, line re-allocation, speed change) that the twin executes over simulated time. Every step can be rolled back.
Slide 12 · Visual Quality and CCTV

Cameras in the twin, quality linked to machine condition

  • Nine cameras: area CCTV, AOI and final inspection, radiometric thermal, dock and stores.
  • Visual QA on a feed with Gemini or the OpenCV vision service on Cloud Run. Every finding waits for a person to confirm or dismiss it.
  • Aligned with IPC-A-610J Class 2, ISO/IEC 15416/15415, ISO 18434-1 and ONVIF; every live view is audited.
Slide 13 · Twin Builder

From a drawing and a description to a running twin

  • Give it a floor plan, P&ID or sketch, requirements in plain words, or an industry template.
  • Read (Gemini multimodal) → Research (Google Search grounding, cited) → Draft → Validate.
  • Every element shows where it came from: blueprint, your requirement, cited source, template, assumption or your edit.
  • Edit directly or by chat; then a deterministic compiler builds the twin with the same engine as the demo.
  • Without AI it says so and starts from the closest of 7 industry templates.
Slide 14 · Playground

Design the plant and its behaviour, then apply

  • Place, move, rotate and delete machines; connect them by dragging between machines; split lines; draw robot routes.
  • Rules: robot movements (output-driven or scheduled trips), connector actions (another line takes over, or slow / pause when packing is blocked), inventory triggers (automatic purchase orders) and maintenance rules (proposals for approval).
  • Undo / redo, live checks, AI help in plain words, and Apply rebuilds the live twin.
Slide 15 · Copilot and MCP

A multi-agent copilot built with Google's Agent Development Kit

Coordinator + specialists

A coordinator delegates to maintenance, quality and planning analysts, each an ADK AgentTool; specialists can run in parallel.

Traceable answers

Every tool call is shown above the answer, and every figure is matched to a tool result; untraceable figures are flagged.

Confirmation gate

propose_plan uses ADK's requireConfirmation. It only creates a pending recommendation, which a person approves.

Slide 17 · Architecture on Google Cloud

System context on Google Cloud

One Next.js service on Firebase App Hosting (Cloud Run) holds the UI, the API, the deterministic engine, the ADK copilot and the MCP server. Language comes from Vertex AI Gemini; computer vision runs as a private Cloud Run service; secrets and settings use Google Cloud's managed services.

Speaker notes: Everything runs in asia-southeast1. The app never holds API keys for Google services: it uses its service account through Application Default Credentials.

Slide 20 · System design principles

System design principles

The architecture follows a small set of rules, applied everywhere and checked by tests.

PrincipleHow TwinForge applies it
Single source of truthOne FactoryState feeds every page, agent, tool and simulation, so no two views can disagree.
Deterministic core, AI at the edgePhysics, forecasts, scores and rankings are pure functions; language models explain, extract and orchestrate, and their output is schema-checked and grounded.
Clean architectureFour layers with one dependency rule: presentation → client state → interface adapters → domain core. Checked on 16 Oct 2026: 202 modules, 728 runtime import edges and no circular imports; the domain imports no framework, server or UI code, and browser code imports nothing from the server.
Ports and adaptersThe domain defines the interfaces it needs (ToolStore, BuilderAi, PipelineDeps); Google Cloud services and AI providers are adapters plugged in at the edge.
Human in the loop by constructionAgents can only create pending proposals; approve, reject and roll back exist only as human actions, and every step is audited.
Commands as dataApproved plans become directives (maintenance window, re-allocation, speed) executed over simulated time, each reversible and audited; Playground edits are validated operations with undo and redo.
Graceful degradationEvery AI feature has a stated fallback (template mode, analysis summary, station-log review); the platform keeps working with AI switched off.
Secure by defaultLeast-privilege service accounts, secrets only on the server, private services behind ID tokens, constant-time secret comparison, validated input on every endpoint.
Testable by designTime and ids are injected; the same engine runs in tests, the browser and the server; demo output is fingerprinted byte for byte.
Performance by architectureThe engine runs in the browser for instant what-if; three.js and heavy effects load only when needed; the plant step is O(machines) per tick.
Slide 21 · SOLID in practice

SOLID in the codebase

PrincipleWhere you can see it
Single responsibility
  • Each domain module does one job: plant physics (world.ts), scenarios and scoring (simulation.ts), recommendations, automation rules, builder edits, validation and compilation.
  • Route handlers are thin: validate with zod → call one domain function → persist → respond; all 46 endpoints share one error contract (400 with field issues, 401, 404, 409, 413, 415).
  • The client has one typed API client, one integrations client and a store per concern (factory, UI, builder, playground, copilot, admin).
Open / closed
  • Registries extend behaviour without editing callers: a tool added to TWIN_TOOLS appears in the ADK copilot and over MCP; an archetype added to ARCHETYPES drives validation, physics, defects and 3D shapes; a setting added to the settings catalogue appears on the Integrations page.
  • Rule kinds and edit operations are discriminated types checked by the compiler.
Liskov substitutionAny ToolStore (the live store or a test fake), any BuilderAi (Gemini, Claude, OpenAI or a recorded fake) and the ProviderLlm adapter (in place of ADK's Gemini model) can replace one another without changes to the code that uses them.
Interface segregationPorts are narrow: ToolStore has three members (get, mutate, now), PipelineDeps three (nowISO, pace, narrate). Components subscribe to narrow store selectors, so a telemetry tick doesn't re-render screens that don't show telemetry.
Dependency inversionThe domain owns the abstractions and imports no framework or cloud SDK; Vertex AI, Cloud Storage, Secret Manager and the vision service are injected at the edge; runtime facts such as serverless detection, the data directory and atomic writes live in one module.

Refactoring for the final build

Two independent architecture audits (domain and server; client and UI) found the strengths above, plus a list of issues. The low-risk, behaviour-preserving fixes were applied before the demo:

Domain and server

  • Business logic moved out of route handlers into domain functions (operator scenarios, recommendation creation, the scripted crisis, camera source switching); an unknown asset now returns 404, not 500.
  • One addRecommendation rule (supersede, add, cap at 20) replaced four copies.
  • DomainError got its own module, and scenario-run bookkeeping moved next to scenarios, so low-level modules no longer import the agent pipeline.
  • One ndjsonResponse helper serves the three streaming endpoints; one runtime module holds environment facts and atomic writes.
  • Shared enums for fault modes, stream kinds and rule kinds; constant-time comparison for the MCP token; the API index lists every route.
  • The floor-layout model moved into the domain and shared wire types into lib/contracts.ts, so the server never imports UI code and the browser never imports server code.

Client and UI

  • One typed integrations client and hook replaced five hand-written fetch calls, three of which could crash on an error response.
  • No component calls fetch directly any more; uploads use one apiForm helper with shared error handling.
  • Duplicated maps (status colours, camera colours, robot and mission labels, machine icons) moved to shared modules; series colours come from the chart kit.
  • Health bands defined once in the domain and used by the status rules, badges, the topology and the asset panel.
  • One highlightFor builder replaced three copies; the guide and the Playground no longer re-render on every telemetry tick.
  • Accessibility: aria-current on navigation, aria-pressed on toggles, client-side links.

Deliberately left for after the demo (larger, riskier changes): table-driven AI-provider and integration registries, a handler table for the 28 edit operations, splitting the client store into slices, and splitting the largest modules.

Slide 22 · Plant engine

A deterministic plant engine powers every number

Physics

  • Machines in series: a line runs at its slowest machine's rate; a down machine stops the line.
  • Wear grows with speed²; crossing the trip threshold causes an unplanned stop.
  • Scrap rises with vibration and is attributed to its cause; materials are consumed per bill of materials.
  • Energy follows speed, idle draw and friction from wear; packed output fills orders by priority, then due time.

Scenario engine

  1. Clone the live state into a simulation.
  2. Calibrate each machine from telemetry (OLS over 6 h plus a change-point test).
  3. Turn plan levers into directives.
  4. Run the plant model in 15-minute steps.
  5. Compute output, downtime, delivery, energy, scrap and cost.
  6. Score against the reference plan: delivery 40, cost 30, risk 20, sustainability 10; plans that run into a trip rank last.

Slide 28 · Security, safety and responsible AI

Safe by construction

No control path to equipment

There is no endpoint or tool that writes to a PLC or machine. Connectors are read-only; approved plans execute in the twin.

People approve

Recommendations from agents, operators or the copilot stay pending until a person approves them. No agent tool can approve, execute or roll back.

Traceable AI

Schema validation, figure-by-figure grounding, provenance on every Twin Builder element, citations from grounding metadata only, and stated fallbacks.

Audit everything

Alerts, findings, scenarios, proposals, decisions, executed actions, camera views and visual reviews are all recorded.

Secrets and access

Secrets stay server-side (Secret Manager, write-only settings). Admin changes need a passcode that unlocks a signed, httpOnly, 8-hour session with rate limiting.

Privacy

Face blur, retention and purpose are recorded per camera, following India's DPDP Act. Video analytics are advisory, never safety functions (IEC 61496 / ISO 13849).

Outbound URLs must use HTTPS and may not carry credentials; the cloud metadata server is refused. Uploads have size and type limits and are never stored.

  • End to end: the full guided crisis demo, the Twin Builder, the Playground, the CCTV control room, MCP, the 3D view and every page rendering without console errors. The suite also runs against the live URL.

Slide 32 · Limitations and roadmap

Honest scope and what comes next

Today

  • The demo runs on a modelled plant with sample data; results are estimates.
  • One factory per deployment; state is held per instance.
  • Machines on a line run in series; positions in the Playground are visual.
  • Camera footage in the demo is licensed video of other facilities.
  • Pub/Sub telemetry works today; OPC UA, Modbus and MQTT come through an edge gateway.

Next

  1. Firestore for shared state, Firebase Auth for sign-in, multiple factories per tenant.
  2. A server-side plant clock with Cloud Scheduler; no instance cap.
  3. Edge gateway for OPC UA, Modbus and MQTT into Pub/Sub; camera analytics at the edge.
  4. Twin Builder self-correction loop on ADK; Agent Engine hosting for the Python agent.
  5. Learned inspection models, validated with a measurement-system study before use.
  6. Agent-to-agent (A2A) endpoint so enterprise agents can delegate to TwinForge.

Glossary

Digital twinA live model of the factory that mirrors its state and can be simulated forward.
OEEOverall equipment effectiveness: availability × performance × quality.
FPY / DPMOFirst-pass yield; defects per million opportunities.
DirectiveAn approved action the twin executes over time: maintenance window, line re-allocation or speed change.
ADKGoogle's Agent Development Kit for building multi-agent systems.
MCPModel Context Protocol: a standard way for AI agents to use tools.
GroundingChecking that every figure an AI states comes from a computed result or a cited source.
AMR / AGVAutonomous mobile robot / automated guided vehicle.
